input: How do I start the game after the initial cutscene?
output: Press the A Button or Start on the title screen. This will lead you through a list of controls and a mission statement from the developers before Professor Oak appears.

input: What are the first things I need to decide for my character?
output: You must select your avatar's gender and a name. The name you choose can be up to seven characters long.

input: How do I enter and edit my character's name?
output: Use the Control Pad to move the cursor and the Select Button to cycle through three pages of characters. Press the A Button to select a letter and the B Button to delete the previous one.

input: How do I finalize my character's name once it is entered?
output: When you are ready, press the Start button. Alternatively, you can select OK in the bottom-right corner of the screen.

input: What happens after I have set up my own character?
output: Professor Oak will introduce his grandson, who serves as your rival. You will then be asked to provide a name for him.

input: How do I name my rival?
output: You can choose a name for the rival from a list of preset names. If you prefer, you may also select a new name for him.

input: Where is Pallet Town located?
output: Pallet Town is situated in the southwest part of the Kanto region. It is described as a small, sleepy town containing only three buildings.

input: What are the three buildings located in Pallet Town?
output: The town features a western house where you and your Mom live and an eastern house where your rival and his sister reside. Additionally, there is a large building to the south which serves as Professor Oak's Laboratory.

input: Where should I go if I want to reach Route 1?
output: To reach Route 1, you should head to the north part of Pallet Town. This area leads directly to the tall grasses of the route.

input: How do I access Route 21 from Pallet Town?
output: You can reach Route 21 by heading to the south part of town. The waters in this direction open up to the route.

input: Who lives in the eastern house of Pallet Town?
output: The eastern house is the home of your rival and his sister. This is one of the three main buildings located within the town.

input: How do I save my progress in the game?
output: Press the Start button to open the main menu and select Save. After selecting Yes, your progress is saved and you can safely exit the game.

input: What are the storage limits for the Bag pockets?
output: The Bag contains three pockets for Items, Key Items, and Poké Balls. Each of these pockets can hold up to 42 different items, with a maximum of 999 for each individual item.

input: What should I do if a Bag pocket becomes full?
output: If a pocket is full, you must use or discard some of your items. This is necessary before you can obtain any new items.

input: How can I get the Potion that is currently in storage?
output: Access the PC and select the Withdraw Item option. From there, choose the Potion to move it from storage into your Bag.

input: What functions does the PC in the bedroom serve?
output: The PC located in the corner of the room serves as your Mailbox. It also acts as your item storage, allowing you to deposit and withdraw items.

input: How many different items can the PC hold?
output: The PC is capable of holding up to 30 different items from the Items pocket.

input: How do I exit the menus to return to my bedroom?
output: You can return to your bedroom by pressing the B Button to close the active menus.

input: What is Mail and how is it used between Trainers?
output: Mail is a type of held item that allows a Trainer to leave a note for another. These messages are sent to other Trainers by trading Pokémon.

input: What happens when a Trainer takes a piece of Mail from a Pokémon?
output: The Trainer can choose to place the Mail in their Bag or send it to their Mailbox. Choosing the Mailbox preserves the original message.

input: Where do I go to leave my bedroom?
output: To go downstairs, you must step on the stairs located in the northeast corner of the room.

input: What does Mom tell you when you see her at the table?
output: Mom informs you that Professor Oak has been looking for you. This serves as your initial prompt to leave the house.

input: How do I leave the house?
output: To exit the house, you must step on the floor mat located along the south wall. Once positioned there, press down on the +Control Pad.

input: What should I do if there is nothing left to explore in Pallet Town and Professor Oak is missing?
output: You should head toward the tall grass located on the north side of town. This action will trigger an encounter with Professor Oak.

input: What happens when you attempt to enter the tall grass on the north side of Pallet Town?
output: Professor Oak will suddenly appear and scold you for trying to venture off on your own. He warns that it is dangerous to go there without a Pokémon for defense.

input: Why does Professor Oak stop you from entering the tall grass?
output: He believes it is dangerous for you to venture out alone. You need a Pokémon of your own to defend yourself against wild Pokémon.

input: Which starter Pokémon is recommended for less experienced Trainers and why?
output: Bulbasaur is a good choice for less experienced Trainers. Its Grass/Poison typing allows it to have an easier time during the early part of the game.

input: What are the strengths and weaknesses of choosing Charmander?
output: Charmander is effective against Bug-, Ice-, Steel-, and Grass-type Pokémon, but it is vulnerable to Ground-, Rock-, and Water-type moves. Because it may struggle early on, it is recommended for players seeking a challenge.

input: How does Squirtle perform against different Pokémon types?
output: Squirtle has an advantage when battling Ground-, Rock-, and Fire-type Pokémon. However, it may struggle when facing Electric- and Grass-type attacks.

input: What should I know about Bulbasaur's type matchups?
output: Bulbasaur does well against Ground-, Rock-, and Water-type Pokémon. It is the most vulnerable of the trio, faring poorly against Ice-, Psychic-, Flying-, and Fire attacks.

input: What happens to Charmander's typing in its final form?
output: When Charmander reaches its final form, Charizard, it gains a secondary Flying type in addition to its Fire type.

input: What is the sequence of events after Oak leads me to his lab?
output: First, you choose your first Pokémon and have the opportunity to nickname it. Then, your rival chooses a Pokémon that has a type advantage over yours. Finally, your rival will challenge you to your first battle as you attempt to leave.

input: How does the rival decide which starter Pokémon to pick?
output: The rival's choice is based on your own selection. He will always choose the Pokémon that possesses a type advantage against the one you picked.

input: Which of the three starter Pokémon is considered the most well-rounded?
output: The Water-type Squirtle is described as the most well-rounded option among the three available starter Pokémon.

input: How do I know the current level and health of the Pokémon in battle?
output: The Pokémon's level is indicated by the Lv5 notation located aside each Pokémon. The remaining HP is displayed on the health bar situated below the level indicator.

input: What determines whether a battle is won or lost?
output: A battle is decided when one side no longer has any Pokémon with the strength to continue. This occurs when all of the opponent's Pokémon have no remaining HP.

input: What is the purpose of the gauge located beneath the health bar?
output: This gauge tracks the amount of Experience Points a Pokémon has accumulated. It shows how many more points are needed for the Pokémon to grow to the next level.

input: What happens when I select the Fight option during a battle?
output: Choosing Fight allows you to launch an attack against the target Pokémon. The professor's Pokémon use either a move that damages the opponent or a move that lowers one of the opponent's stats.

input: What should I do if my Pokémon's HP becomes low during the fight?
output: You should use the Potion that was obtained from your PC. To do this, navigate to the Item menu to select the medicine and apply it to your Pokémon.

input: What are the rewards for defeating Blue?
output: After defeating Blue, you will receive a cash reward of $80. Additionally, your Pokémon will earn enough Experience Points to grow to Level 6.

input: Where should I go after the battle with Blue is finished?
output: Once Blue leaves, you should exit the laboratory. From there, head north to reach Route 1.

input: Where does Route 1 lead and where does it start?
output: Route 1 is a country road that begins in Pallet Town. It leads the player north toward Viridian City.

input: What obstacles are found on Route 1 that make traveling north difficult?
output: The path on Route 1 is filled with patches of tall grass. Additionally, there are one-way ledges that hinder northward travel.

input: Can I catch wild Pokémon on Route 1?
output: No, it is not yet possible to catch any of the wild Pokémon found here. However, you should still battle them to earn valuable Experience Points.

input: What is the benefit of battling wild Pokémon on Route 1 if they cannot be caught?
output: While you cannot catch the wild Pokémon on this route, battling them is still beneficial. Doing so allows you to earn valuable Experience Points.

input: Where can I find the man who gives out free samples?
output: You can find this man on the south side of the route. He is located near the signpost.

input: What happens when you speak to the man near the signpost on the south side of the route?
output: The man will give you a Potion as a free sample. He explains that he works at the Poké Mart in Viridian City.

input: Who provides a free Potion on the south side of the route?
output: A man who works at the Viridian City Poké Mart provides the item. He can be found standing near the signpost.

input: Where is Viridian City located?
output: Viridian City is situated between Route 1 to the south and Route 2 to the north. Additionally, Route 22 can be found to the west of the city.

input: What is the environment of Viridian City like?
output: Viridian City is a small city that loves nature. Because of this, the city remains enveloped in green throughout the entire year.

input: What services are provided at the Pokémon Center?
output: The Pokémon Center acts as a hospital that restores your team to full health and removes any status ailments. Additionally, it provides a PC that allows Trainers to manage their item and Pokémon storage.

input: How does the Pokémon storage system work for Trainers?
output: Trainers are limited to carrying only six Pokémon at one time. Any additional Pokémon captured are automatically transferred into storage.

input: What should I do when I encounter a Pokémon Center?
output: You should use the facility to heal your team to full health. It is also recommended that you save your progress while visiting the center.

input: Where can a Trainer access their item storage?
output: Item storage can be accessed via the PC located within the Pokémon Center. This facility is the first building you will encounter.

input: Where is the local Poké Mart located?
output: The Poké Mart is situated to the northeast of the Pokémon Center. You can find it in this area to purchase necessary supplies.

input: What items can be purchased at the Poké Mart?
output: These stores provide a variety of items for the player. Specifically, you can buy different types of Poké Balls and Potions.

input: What is the recommended strategy regarding supplies at the Poké Mart?
output: It is a good idea to stock up on supplies whenever you have the opportunity. This is recommended because you cannot predict what you might encounter during your journey.

input: What happens when you enter the shop?
output: The shopkeeper recognizes you as a resident of Pallet Town and calls you over to the counter. He informs you that a delivery arrived for Professor Oak.

input: What item do you receive from the shopkeeper?
output: The shopkeeper gives you Oak's Parcel. You are asked to take this item to Professor Oak.

input: Can you buy items from the shopkeeper immediately?
output: No, you cannot make any purchases at this time. The shopkeeper is adamant that you must complete the delivery before you can buy anything.

input: What must you do before you are allowed to make purchases at the shop?
output: You must first take Oak's Parcel to Professor Oak. The shopkeeper will not allow you to buy items until this delivery is made.

input: Where is the Pokémon academy located and what is its purpose?
output: The Pokémon academy is situated in the center of the city. It is designed to teach inexperienced Trainers the fundamental basics of battle.

input: What information can be found on the blackboard in the Pokémon academy?
output: There is a blackboard located in the front of the room. It provides a description of the five status ailments that can affect a Pokémon.

input: What is the first thing I need to do for Professor Oak?
output: You must deliver Oak's Parcel, which is a custom Poké Ball, to the professor. Once you have done this, Blue will arrive shortly after.

input: What is the Pokédex and how does it work?
output: The Pokédex is a high-tech encyclopedia invented by Professor Oak that records data on every Pokémon you encounter. It will be considered complete once you have caught a member of every species.

input: Why is Professor Oak asking the player and Blue to gather information on Pokémon?
output: It was Professor Oak's dream to gather information on all the Pokémon in the world himself. However, because of his advanced age, he must rely on you and Blue to complete this task.

input: What items does Professor Oak provide to help the player get started?
output: To assist you in your journey, Professor Oak gives five Poké Balls to both you and Blue.

input: What is the ultimate goal of using the Pokédex?
output: The goal is to use the device to gather information on all the Pokémon in the world. This is achieved by encountering and catching a member of every species.

input: What should I do before leaving town?
output: You should visit your rival's house. While there, speak to his sister, Daisy, to obtain a Town Map.

input: How do I get a Town Map?
output: Go to your rival's house before you leave town. Speak with Daisy, who is your rival's sister, to receive the item.

input: Who gives the player the Town Map and where can they be found?
output: The Town Map is given by Daisy. She can be found at your rival's house.

input: What can I do at the Poké Mart now that Oak's Parcel has been delivered?
output: Once you have delivered Oak's Parcel, you are now able to purchase items at the Poké Mart.

input: How do I get past the old man who was blocking the path northward?
output: You can now pass the old man because he is feeling better after having his coffee. When you pass him, he will notice your Pokédex and demonstrate how to catch a Pokémon.

input: What item does the old man give me and what is its purpose?
output: The old man gives you the Teachy TV, which is a portable device. It is tuned to the Poké Dude Show, a program hosted by his grandson that teaches the basics of being a Pokémon Trainer.

input: Where can I go after passing the old man?
output: You have two options for your next destination. You may proceed north to Route 2, or you can take an optional detour westward to Route 22.

input: What can I do on Route 22 even though it cannot be fully explored yet?
output: While you cannot fully explore Route 22 at this time, you can still use the area to hunt for new Pokémon. Additionally, you will encounter Blue shortly after entering the route.

input: What happens when I enter Route 22?
output: As you travel a short distance into Route 22, Blue will appear. He will then challenge you to a battle.

input: What change has occurred in Professor Oak's team since the previous fight?
output: Professor Oak has added a Pidgey to his team. This addition is particularly dangerous for trainers who chose Bulbasaur, as Pidgey can use Gust to deal serious damage to Grass Pokémon.

input: What strategy should I use to defeat Professor Oak?
output: You should employ the same tactics used during your last battle with him. Focus on wearing his Pokémon down to secure the victory.

input: What should I do immediately after winning the battle against Professor Oak?
output: Once the battle is over, make sure to heal your Pokémon. You should also stock up on Poké Balls before continuing your journey to Route 2.

input: What can I do if I have no Poké Balls and defeated Blue before catching any Pokémon?
output: You can return to Pallet Town and speak with Professor Oak. He will provide you with 5 Poké Balls if you meet these conditions.

input: How do I get from Viridian City to Pewter City?
output: You must travel northward along Route 2. This path connects the two cities, though parts of the route are occupied by a forest or blocked by trees.

input: What is the large maze of trees on the west side of Route 2 called?
output: The maze of trees located on the west side of the route is known as Viridian Forest. You can enter this area through a gate to find new Pokémon to catch.

input: Can I access the east side of Route 2?
output: No, access to the east side of the route is currently blocked. This is due to the presence of overgrown trees.

input: Where should I go if I want to find new Pokémon to catch after leaving Viridian City?
output: You should head through the gate to enter Viridian Forest. This is a whole new area located on the west side of Route 2.

input: How do I find the Poké Ball in Viridian Forest?
output: From the entrance of the forest, follow the trail toward the northwest. You will find the Poké Ball located within the tall grass in that area.

input: Where can I find the Potions located within Viridian Forest?
output: One Potion is located in a grass patch in the southeastern part of the forest. A second Potion can be found by exploring a dead-end path to the southeast after reaching the signpost.

input: What is the sequence of events for navigating the eastern side of the forest?
output: First, head eastward from the entrance to find a Potion. Then, turn north to battle Bug Catcher Rick and continue past Bug Catcher Doug to collect an Antidote.

input: What should I do after collecting the Antidote near Bug Catcher Doug?
output: Turn west into the tall grass and zigzag through the trees. This path will eventually lead you to a signpost.

input: How do I exit Viridian Forest and reach Pewter City?
output: Defeat Bug Catcher Sammy to reach the northern edge of the forest. Exit through the gate to return to Route 2, then continue traveling north to arrive at Pewter City.

input: Which Bug Catchers will I encounter while navigating Viridian Forest?
output: You will encounter Bug Catcher Rick on the east side of the forest. Later, you will pass Bug Catcher Doug and eventually defeat Bug Catcher Sammy near the northern edge.

input: Where is the Antidote located in the forest?
output: The Antidote is found on the east side of the forest. It is located near Bug Catcher Doug, whom you pass after battling Bug Catcher Rick.

input: Where is Pewter City located?
output: Pewter City is a quiet city situated in the northern mountains. It is positioned between Route 2 and Route 3.

input: What points of interest can be found in Pewter City?
output: There are two primary locations in the city. You can visit the Pewter Museum of Science and the Pewter Gym.

input: How can I find the local Gym Leader?
output: You should attempt to leave the city through the east exit. A kid blocking the path will then escort you to the Gym.

input: What happens if I try to leave the city via the east exit?
output: You will encounter a kid who is blocking the exit. This NPC will offer to escort you to the local Gym Leader, who is currently looking for challengers.

input: Where is the Pewter Museum of Science located?
output: The Pewter Museum of Science is situated on the north side of the city. It is a facility that hosts various exhibits and artifacts.

input: What are the primary focuses of the exhibits at the Pewter Museum of Science?
output: The museum's exhibits focus specifically on space exploration and fossil excavation. It hosts a wide range of artifacts related to these topics.

input: How much does it cost for a child to enter the main building of the museum?
output: Admission to the main building costs $50 for a child's ticket. This fee grants access to the museum's artifacts and exhibits.

input: Can I enter the smaller building located next to the Pewter Museum of Science?
output: No, you cannot enter the smaller building. The passage states that this specific building is closed to the public.

input: What are the type strengths and weaknesses of the Pokémon in the Pewter Gym?
output: The gym specializes in Rock-type Pokémon, which are super effective against Bug, Fire, Flying, and Ice types. However, they are weak to Fighting, Grass, Ground, Steel, and Water moves. Because they are also partly Ground type, they are immune to Electric attacks.

input: Which starter Pokémon are best suited for the battle against Brock, and why?
output: Bulbasaur and Squirtle are the best choices because Brock's Pokémon are part-Rock and part-Ground. This specific type combination causes them to take massive damage from Grass and Water attacks.

input: Why might a trainer with Charmander struggle against Brock's Pokémon?
output: Although Geodude and Onix have low Special Defense, their type combination resists damage from Fire moves. This makes Fire attacks less effective for Charmander during the battle.

input: What is a recommended strategy for using Charmander to defeat Brock?
output: You should raise Charmander to level 13 so it can learn Metal Claw. This Steel-type move deals serious damage to Rock Pokémon and has the potential to raise Charmander's physical Attack.

input: If I am struggling with the Pewter Gym, where can I find a helpful Pokémon to assist me?
output: You can find the Fighting-type Pokémon Mankey on Route 22. Mankey is a useful alternative because it learns both Karate Chop and Low Kick early on.

input: What rewards do I receive after defeating Brock?
output: Brock awards you the Boulder Badge and TM39, which contains the move Rock Tomb. These prizes are given to the player immediately after the battle.

input: What are the specific benefits of obtaining the Boulder Badge?
output: The Boulder Badge provides your Pokémon with a slight Attack boost during battles. Additionally, it enables the use of Flash while you are in the field.

input: Where should I go after defeating the Pewter Gym?
output: Your next destination is Cerulean City, which is located to the east. Once you arrive, you can visit the Poké Mart to stock up on essential items.

input: What items are recommended for purchase at the Cerulean City Poké Mart?
output: You should buy Potions and Poké Balls for general use. Additionally, consider getting an Escape Rope or two and some Repels to prepare for the cave ahead.

input: How do I obtain the Running Shoes?
output: Head east to Route 3. At the edge of the city, you will be stopped by one of Professor Oak's aides who is delivering the shoes from your Mom.

input: How do the Running Shoes work in the game?
output: The Running Shoes allow you to move faster than normal. To activate this speed boost, you must hold down the B Button while moving.

input: What is the sequence of events for leaving Cerulean City?
output: First, visit the Poké Mart to prepare for the upcoming cave. Then, head east toward Route 3, where you will meet an aide of Professor Oak to receive the Running Shoes.

input: Where does Route 3 lead?
output: Route 3 is a grassy road that leads east from Pewter City. It takes the player into the mountains that surround Route 4.

input: What can a player expect to encounter while traveling along Route 3?
output: You will find many Trainers along this path. These Trainers are present because they are raising their Pokémon in preparation for the upcoming cave.

input: Where can I find the man selling Magikarp?
output: You can find a shady man inside the Pokémon Center located near the entrance to Mt. Moon. He offers to sell you a Magikarp for $500.

input: Is it worth buying the Magikarp from the shady man?
output: Buying the fish allows you to obtain a strong Water-type Pokémon sooner than normal if you have the money. However, you can eventually catch a Magikarp for free if you have the correct fishing rod.

input: What happens to Magikarp as it levels up?
output: Magikarp is nearly useless in its initial form. Once it reaches level 20, it evolves into the powerful Gyarados.

input: What can be found at Mt. Moon due to its frequent meteor falls?
output: Mt. Moon is known for frequent meteor falls. The shards of stars that fall at this location are known as Moon Stones.

input: Which Pokémon can be encountered within Mt. Moon?
output: Several cave-dwelling Pokémon make their home in the mountain. Specifically, you can find Zubat and Paras here.

input: What should I expect to encounter while exploring the tunnels of Mt. Moon?
output: While exploring the tunnels, you will find many Trainers. You will also encounter cave-dwelling Pokémon such as Paras and Zubat.

input: What items should I collect before heading east through the tunnel?
output: You should collect TM09 (Bullet Seed) and the Parlyz Heal. These items are located to the west before you proceed eastward through the tunnel.

input: What are the steps for navigating the tunnel after collecting the items to the west?
output: After gathering the items, follow the tunnel in an eastward direction. Once you have moved east, climb down the first ladder you encounter.

input: What should I do after defeating the Team Rocket Grunt?
output: Once you have battled the Team Rocket Grunt, head to the raised platform to collect the Star Piece. After grabbing the item, use the ladder to return to the first floor.

input: How do I get back to the first floor after finding the Star Piece?
output: Locate the ladder after you have retrieved the Star Piece from the raised platform. Use this ladder to travel back down to 1F.

input: What is the correct sequence of events for this area?
output: First, you must engage in a battle with the Team Rocket Grunt. Next, retrieve the Star Piece from the raised platform before taking the ladder back to 1F.

input: What should I do after battling the next two Trainers?
output: After the battles, make sure to collect the Escape Rope, Rare Candy, and Potion. Then, head north and west before climbing down the second ladder.

input: Which items can be found in this area?
output: You can collect a Potion, a Rare Candy, and an Escape Rope. These items are located along the path where you battle the next two Trainers.

input: What is the correct sequence of movements to reach the second ladder?
output: First, go south to fight two Trainers and collect the available items. Afterward, travel north and then west to find and climb down the second ladder.

input: What should I do after fighting the second Team Rocket Grunt?
output: Once you have defeated the second Team Rocket Grunt, pick up TM46 (Thief) from the platform. Afterward, inspect the large rock to find a hidden Ether before you head back to 1F.

input: Where can I find TM46 (Thief) in this area?
output: TM46 (Thief) can be found on a platform. You can collect it after you have fought the second Team Rocket Grunt.

input: How do I obtain the hidden Ether?
output: To get the hidden Ether, you must inspect the large rock. This should be done before you return to 1F.

input: What is the correct sequence of events to follow in this section?
output: First, fight the second Team Rocket Grunt and collect TM46 (Thief) from the platform. Next, inspect the large rock to locate a hidden Ether, and then return to 1F.

input: What should I do after continuing westward along the tunnel?
output: First, head to the northwest corner to collect the Moon Stone. After grabbing the item, locate and take the third ladder to reach the lower floor.

input: Where can I find the Moon Stone in the tunnel?
output: The Moon Stone is located in the northwest corner of the tunnel. You can find it by continuing westward through the area.

input: How do I get to the lower floor of the tunnel?
output: Continue westward through the tunnel and locate the third ladder. Using this ladder will allow you to descend to the lower floor.

input: How do I find the fossils in the tunnel?
output: Follow the winding tunnel in a clockwise direction toward the northwest. There, you will find Super Nerd Miguel, who has claimed the Dome Fossil and Helix Fossil as his own.

input: What must I do to obtain a fossil from Super Nerd Miguel?
output: You must engage in a battle and defeat Super Nerd Miguel. Once he is defeated, he will allow you to choose either the Dome Fossil or the Helix Fossil for yourself.

input: What are the Dome Fossil and Helix Fossil?
output: The Dome Fossil was once a Pokémon known as Kabuto. The Helix Fossil was once a Pokémon known as Omanyte.

input: What should I do after defeating Super Nerd Miguel and picking a fossil?
output: Continue moving forward to collect an Antidote. From there, climb the final ladder to reach the exit.

input: Where can I find the Black Belt Move Tutors?
output: You can find two Black Belts training on the western hill. These NPCs serve as Move Tutors for compatible Pokémon.

input: Which moves can be learned from the Black Belts on the western hill?
output: The man on the left is able to teach Mega Punch to a compatible Pokémon. The man on the right can teach Mega Kick.

input: How many times can I use the services of the Black Belt Move Tutors?
output: The services provided by these Move Tutors may only be used once. This limitation applies to both the man teaching Mega Punch and the man teaching Mega Kick.

input: What is the function of the Black Belts found on the western hill?
output: These men act as Move Tutors. They are capable of teaching their respective moves to Pokémon that are compatible.

input: Where is Cerulean City located?
output: Cerulean City is situated between Route 4, Route 24, Route 9, and Route 5. It is described as a beautiful city featuring blooming flowers and flowing water.

input: How can I obtain a Jynx from the old man?
output: Go to the house located next to the Pokémon Center to find the old man. He will trade you his Jynx if you provide him with a Poliwhirl.

input: What is required to get a Poliwhirl for trading?
output: You must use a high-level fishing rod to find a Poliwhirl. This Pokémon is necessary if you wish to trade with the old man for his Jynx.

input: Where is the NPC who trades a Jynx located?
output: The old man is located in the house situated next to the Pokémon Center. He is the NPC willing to trade his Jynx for a Poliwhirl.

input: What can I learn from the man in the northwest house?
output: The man in the northwest house provides an explanation regarding the effects of the eight Gym Badges. He details how these badges impact your Pokémon's performance and utility.

input: What are the different effects of the Gym Badges?
output: Four of the badges provide a slight boost to a specific stat, while the other four ensure that your Pokémon remain obedient during battle. Additionally, the first seven badges are required to unlock the use of field moves.

input: How do Gym Badges affect a Pokémon's obedience?
output: Half of the eight Gym Badges are designed to ensure a Pokémon's obedience during battle. The other half of the badges instead provide slight power boosts to respective stats.

input: Which Gym Badges are necessary to use field moves?
output: You must obtain the first seven Gym Badges to unlock the use of field moves. This is one of the various effects explained by the man in the northwest house.

input: What can the old man in the north-northwest house do for the player?
output: The old man is capable of concocting a variety of medicines. To receive these, you must provide him with the required amount of Berry Powder.

input: What item is given to the player during their first visit to the old man's house?
output: On your first visit, the old man gives you the Powder Jar. This item is used to store all Berry Powder that you obtain from the Berry Crush minigame.

input: How does a player obtain the Powder Jar and what is its purpose?
output: You obtain the Powder Jar by visiting the old man in the north-northwest house for the first time. Once acquired, it stores any Berry Powder collected through the Berry Crush minigame.

input: Where can I find the Bike Shop and what is available there?
output: The Bike Shop is located in the southwest part of town. You can purchase a Bicycle from this shop.

input: How much does a Bicycle cost at the Bike Shop?
output: A Bicycle costs $1,000,000. Because it is not possible to carry that much money, you cannot purchase one at this time.

input: Can I buy a Bicycle to speed up my travel?
output: No, you are stuck traveling on foot for now. The Bicycle costs $1,000,000, which is more money than you are able to carry.

input: What is happening at the house in the northeast?
output: The house is currently blocked off by a police officer. Team Rocket has broken into the home and stolen a valuable item from the residents.

input: Can I enter the house in the northeast right now?
output: No, you cannot enter the house at this time because it is blocked by a police officer. There is currently nothing that can be done to remedy the situation.

input: Where should I go since the house in the northeast is blocked?
output: Since you cannot access the house, you should set your sights on the Gym instead. This is the recommended next destination while the house remains inaccessible.

input: What are the strengths and weaknesses of Water-type Pokémon?
output: Water-type moves are super effective when used against Rock-, Ground-, and Fire-type Pokémon. Conversely, Water-type Pokémon are weak to moves of the Grass and Electric types.

input: How should I handle Misty's Staryu and Starmie in the Cerulean Gym?
output: You should defeat Staryu quickly so you can move on to Starmie. Because Starmie is faster and stronger, use Grass moves like Bullet Seed and Vine Whip or Pikachu's ThunderShock to deal serious damage.

input: Why is Misty's Starmie particularly dangerous?
output: Starmie is both faster and stronger than Staryu. This makes its Water Pulse move especially painful for Pokémon that are vulnerable to it.

input: What rewards do I receive after defeating Misty?
output: Misty will award you the Cascade Badge and TM03, which contains the move Water Pulse. These prizes are given to you after the battle concludes.

input: What are the benefits of obtaining the Cascade Badge?
output: The Cascade Badge allows you to use Cut while in the field. Additionally, it ensures that all Pokémon up to level 30 will obey you.

input: Which specific moves are recommended for defeating Misty's Pokémon?
output: To make quick work of her team, use Pikachu's ThunderShock. Alternatively, you can use Grass-type moves such as Bullet Seed and Vine Whip.

input: What is the best strategy for defeating Blue's Pidgeotto?
output: You should use Rock-type and Electric-type attacks against Pidgeotto. Be careful not to use your first Pokémon in this fight, as Pidgeotto now has a same-type attack that deals 50% more damage and could cause serious harm.

input: How should I handle Blue's Abra during the battle?
output: Abra is a sitting duck because its only move does not deal any damage. This makes it an ideal opportunity to gain experience for your lower-leveled Pokémon.

input: What should I be aware of when fighting Blue's Rattata?
output: Rattata uses Quick Attack, which allows it to move first regardless of its Speed stat. You should try to defeat it quickly to mitigate this advantage.

input: What happens after the battle with Blue?
output: Blue will initially brag about visiting a world-famous PokéManiac to gather Pokédex data before running off. He then returns shortly after to give you a gift because he feels sorry for you.

input: What is the Fame Checker and how do you get it?
output: The Fame Checker is a device used to record miscellaneous information about famous people, such as Gym Leaders. You receive this item as a gift from Blue after your battle near Route 24.

input: Where can I go once Blue leaves for the second time?
output: After Blue gives you the Fame Checker and departs, you are free to continue your journey toward Route 24.

input: Where is Route 24 located?
output: Route 24 is located north of Cerulean City. It extends from the city up to Route 25.

input: What are the primary features found on Route 24?
output: The majority of Route 24 is occupied by a river. Additionally, the Nugget Bridge is located here to cross over the water.

input: What must I do to receive a Nugget on Nugget Bridge?
output: You need to fight and defeat all five Trainers located on the bridge. Once this is accomplished, a man at the north end of the bridge will reward you with the Nugget.

input: What is the value of the Nugget found on Nugget Bridge?
output: The Nugget is described as a bit of gold. It can be sold for a high price.

input: What happens after the man at the north end of Nugget Bridge gives me the Nugget?
output: The man reveals that he is actually a Team Rocket Grunt. He will attempt to persuade you to join Team Rocket and will start a battle if you refuse.

input: How many Trainers are located on Nugget Bridge?
output: There are five Trainers to be fought on Nugget Bridge. Defeating all of them is required to get a reward from the man at the north end.

input: How do I get to Route 25?
output: To reach Route 25, you must travel eastward from Route 24. The path will then wind through a forest area.

input: Where is the Sea Cottage located?
output: The Sea Cottage is situated on the east side of Route 25. This is the area where the path ends overlooking the sea.

input: What is the geography of Route 25?
output: Route 25 consists of a path that winds through a forest. It eventually ends at a point that overlooks the sea.

input: Who owns the Sea Cottage and what is his profession?
output: The Sea Cottage is owned by Bill. He is a famous Pokémon researcher.

input: What has happened to Bill when you find him at the Sea Cottage?
output: Bill's latest experiment went awry, resulting in his DNA being combined with that of a Pokémon. Because of this, he appears as a Pokémon inside the cottage.

input: How do you help Bill return to his normal human form?
output: First, wait for Bill to step into the machine. Then, inspect his PC to activate a program that will undo the change.

input: What reward do you receive for helping Bill, and what does it do?
output: Bill gives you an S.S. Ticket as a token of gratitude. This ticket grants you access to the luxury cruise ship docked in Vermilion City.

input: Where should you go to use the S.S. Ticket?
output: You should travel south to Vermilion City. The luxury cruise ship is currently docked there.

input: What can you do with Bill's PC before leaving the cape?
output: You can exit and re-enter the cottage to inspect Bill's PC. Doing this allows you to view some of his favorite Pokémon.

input: How does inspecting Bill's PC affect your Pokédex?
output: Inspecting the PC to view Bill's favorite Pokémon updates your progress. This action adds four new pages to your Pokédex.

input: What should I do once I return to Cerulean City to find the thief?
output: Go to the burgled house, as the officer blocking the entrance has now stepped aside. Once inside, locate the large hole in the wall and step through it to confront the thief.

input: How do I obtain TM28 (Dig)?
output: You must find and defeat the Rocket Grunt located outside the hole in the wall of the burgled house in Cerulean City. Upon his defeat, the Grunt will give up the TM28 before fleeing.

input: What is the effect of using Dig inside a cave?
output: Using Dig while inside a cave will instantly return you to the entrance. This is a useful strategy when you are in a pinch and need to heal your Pokémon.

input: Where does Route 5 lead?
output: Route 5 is a scenic road that runs downhill. It connects Cerulean City to Saffron City.

input: Where can I find the first Underground Path in the region?
output: The first of the region's two Underground Paths begins on Route 5. From there, it runs southward underneath Saffron City.

input: How do I get to Route 6 using the Underground Path?
output: You can enter the Underground Path on Route 5. Follow the path southward underneath Saffron City to re-emerge on Route 6.

input: What is the purpose of the house on the hill?
output: The house on the hill serves as the Pokémon Day Care. Inside, an old man will raise one of your Pokémon for you while you are away.

input: How does a Pokémon gain experience while at the Day Care?
output: A Pokémon left at the Day Care earns one experience point for every step you take. This makes it a useful method for raising a Pokémon like the Magikarp bought near Mt. Moon.

input: What is the risk of leaving a Pokémon at the Day Care?
output: The downside is that the old man makes all the decisions for the Pokémon. Consequently, he might delete a move that you would prefer to keep.

input: How much does it cost to get a Pokémon back from the Day Care?
output: Returning a Pokémon costs an initial fee of $100. Additionally, you must pay another $100 for every new level the Pokémon has gained.

input: What should I do if I cannot reach Saffron City?
output: Since it is currently impossible to reach Saffron City, you should enter the Underground Path. From there, follow the tunnel until you arrive at Route 6.

input: How do I get to Route 6 when Saffron City is inaccessible?
output: You can reach Route 6 by using the Underground Path. Enter the path and follow the tunnel to complete the journey.

input: Where can I find a girl willing to trade Nidoran?
output: You can find a girl looking to trade in the north gate. She is offering either a Nidoran♀ or a Nidoran♂ depending on what you have.

input: What are the requirements to trade with the girl in the north gate?
output: To trade with this NPC, you must provide the opposite-gender counterpart of the Nidoran she is offering. For example, you must trade a Nidoran♂ to receive a Nidoran♀, or vice versa.

input: What item is received when trading with the girl in the north gate?
output: The Pokémon you receive from this trade will be holding a TinyMushroom. This item arrives with the Nidoran♀ or Nidoran♂.

input: How do I catch wild Pokémon in the game?
output: You can find wild Pokémon in bodies of water, caves, and tall grass. To successfully catch these creatures, you will need to utilize various types of Poké Balls.

input: What happens to wild Pokémon as they are trained?
output: While wild caught Pokémon start out weak, they become progressively stronger through training. Some may also evolve, which typically provides them with a new look, new moves, and higher stats.

input: Where can I find wild Pokémon to catch?
output: Wild Pokémon are located in several different environments. You should look for them in tall grass, caves, and bodies of water.

input: What are the benefits of a Pokémon evolving?
output: When a Pokémon is capable of evolving, doing so generally grants it higher stats. Additionally, evolution provides the Pokémon with new moves and a new appearance.

input: How do reappearing items work in certain areas of the game?
output: Certain areas contain items that reappear over time, which are divided into common, uncommon, and rare groups. These items always appear in the same locations, although some areas may have empty groups.

input: What triggers the reshuffling of reappearing items?
output: Reappearing items are reshuffled and placed after the player has walked 1500 steps. The new items are then placed based on the group chosen for that specific area.

input: What are the probabilities for which group of reappearing items will be selected?
output: There is a 60% chance that the common group will be selected. The uncommon group has a 30% chance, while the rare group has a 10% chance.

input: How can I re-challenge trainers that I have already encountered in the world?
output: You can re-challenge trainers that are found in the world by using the Vs. Seeker. This item allows you to engage in battles with them again.

input: Where can I find information regarding major characters like Gym Leaders?
output: Information on major characters, including Gym Leaders, is stored in the Fame Checker. You can access this tool to review details about these specific individuals.

input: How do I obtain the National Mode for the Pokédex?
output: To unlock National Mode, you must first defeat The Elite Four. Additionally, you need to catch 60 different Pokémon, which can include evolving your existing Pokémon.

input: What content is added to the Pokédex once National Mode is active?
output: Activating National Mode expands the Pokédex to include all Pokémon from the Johto and Hoenn regions.

input: Does evolving Pokémon count toward the requirement for National Mode?
output: Yes, evolving your Pokémon counts toward the goal of catching 60 different Pokémon. This is one of the requirements needed alongside beating The Elite Four to unlock National Mode.

input: What is required for a Pokémon to undergo a Generation II or III evolution, such as Golbat evolving into Crobat?
output: You must first obtain the National Pokédex. Without this item, Pokémon are unable to evolve into their Generation II and III forms.

input: Where can I breed my Pokémon?
output: You can breed your Pokémon at the daycare located on Four Island. Additionally, Pokémon can still be placed in the daycare on Route 5.

input: How do I find Moltres and when is it accessible?
output: Moltres is located on Mt. Ember, which is a volcano on One Island. You can only access this location after you have defeated the 7th Gym on Cinnabar Island.

input: How can I obtain one of the Legendary Beasts, and which one will I find?
output: After defeating the Elite Four once, Entei, Raikou, or Suicune may appear randomly in the tall grass of the Kanto Region. The specific beast available is determined by the starter Pokémon you chose at the start of the game.

input: What are the requirements to catch Lugia or Ho-Oh?
output: You must have defeated the Elite Four and obtained the event item called the MysticTicket. Once you have the ticket, you can access their locations by going to the harbor.

input: How do I catch Deoxys and in what form will it appear?
output: You must obtain the event item Aurora Ticket and then go to the harbor to access its location. Deoxys will be in Attack Form in FireRed and Defense Form in LeafGreen.

input: Where can I find Articuno and Zapdos?
output: Articuno can be found at the Seafoam Islands. Zapdos is located at the Power Plant.

input: Where is Mewtwo located?
output: Mewtwo remains located in Cerulean Cave.

input: Has the typing for Magnemite changed?
output: Yes, certain Pokémon have had their types changed. Magnemite is now an Electric/Steel type.

input: What attributes do Pokémon have in this game besides their species?
output: Pokémon possess Natures, Abilities, and Genders. They are also capable of holding items.

input: Which moves are exclusive to starter Pokémon and where can they be learned?
output: Starter Pokémon can learn the new moves Blast Burn, Frenzy Plant, and Hydro Cannon. These specific moves are available from a Move Tutor located on Two Island.

input: What version of the TM list is used in Fire Red and Leaf Green?
output: The games utilize the Generation III TM list. They do not use the Generation I list.

input: How can a player teach their Pokémon Generation I TMs?
output: You can use Move Tutors to teach your Pokémon these moves. Move Tutors are now available for this purpose.

input: What updates have been made to Pokémon movesets?
output: Movesets have been updated to include moves that were added in Generations II and III.

input: Which GBA games can I trade with?
output: You can trade with other Game Boy Advance titles. Specifically, you can trade with Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire, and Emerald.

input: How can I trade with Pokémon Colosseum or Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness?
output: You must connect your Game Boy Advance to a GameCube. This is done using a GBA Link Cable.

input: What is required to obtain the National Pokédex Certificate?
output: To get this certificate, you must perform trades between all the mentioned games. This includes the GBA titles and the GameCube titles.

input: Where is Team Rocket's new base located?
output: Team Rocket has established a new base on Five Island. This makes them the only villainous team to remain active after the Elite Four.

input: When can the Elite Four be re-challenged?
output: The Elite Four are available to be challenged again after the initial completion. This allows the player to face them once more.

input: What happens to the Elite Four's roster after completing the Sapphire quest at the Sevii Islands?
output: Once the Sapphire quest at the Sevii Islands is finished, the Elite Four will update their teams. Their rosters will then include both Generation I and Generation II Pokémon.

input: What factors determine whether a Pokémon wins or loses a battle?
output: Victory or defeat in battles is determined by the Pokémon's moves, types, and stats. These elements make the critical difference during combat.

input: What should a player do before summoning a Pokémon to the battlefield?
output: You should carefully consider the characteristics of each Pokémon before sending it out. This preparation is important for ensuring success in battle.

input: How do I interpret the numbers in the type matchup chart?
output: A '2' indicates that a move is doubly effective, while a '1/2' means effectiveness is reduced by half. A '0' signifies that the move will produce no damage at all against that Pokémon type.

input: What happens if there is a blank spot in the type matchup chart?
output: A blank spot indicates that a move of that particular type is neither effective nor ineffective. It deals neutral damage to a Pokémon of the other type.

input: How are type matchups calculated for a Pokémon with two different types?
output: Pokémon with two types are subject to the resistances, immunities, and weaknesses of both types. These effects can combine to increase or cancel each other out.

input: Why is Dragonite 4x weak to Ice-type attacks?
output: Dragonite is a Dragon- and Flying-type Pokémon. Because both the Dragon and Flying types are weak to Ice, the weakness is compounded to 4x.

input: Why is Dragonite 4x resistant to Grass-type attacks?
output: Dragonite possesses both the Dragon and Flying types. Since both of these types are resistant to Grass, it receives a 4x resistance.

input: How does Dragonite react to Electric-type attacks?
output: Dragonite is neutral against Electric-type attacks. This occurs because its Flying-type weakness and Dragon-type resistance cancel each other out.

input: What is the 'same-type attack bonus' (STAB)?
output: STAB is a 50% power increase provided to attacks that are the same type as the Pokémon using them. For example, a Water-type Seel will be more effective using the Water-type move Surf than a non-Water-type like Nidoking.

input: Do dual-type Pokémon receive STAB for both of their types?
output: Yes, Pokémon with two types receive STAB for both. An example is Dewgong, a Water- and Ice-type, which receives the bonus for both the Water-type move Surf and the Ice-type move Aurora Beam.

input: What are the six main stats that determine a Pokemon's capabilities in battle?
output: The six main stats are HP, Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def, and Speed. These values collectively determine how a Pokemon performs during battle.

input: Which stats influence the strength and damage of physical attacks?
output: The Attack stat determines how strong a Pokemon's physical attacks are. Conversely, the Defense stat determines how much damage the Pokemon takes from those physical attacks.

input: How do Special Attack and Special Defense affect battle performance?
output: The Sp. Atk (Special Attack) stat determines the strength of a Pokemon's special attacks. The Sp. Def (Special Defense) stat determines how much damage the Pokemon takes from special attacks.

input: What is the function of the HP stat?
output: The HP stat determines the amount of damage a Pokemon can sustain. Once this limit is reached, the Pokemon will faint.

input: What role does the Speed stat play in battle, and are there any exceptions?
output: Speed determines the strength of Special attacks and the amount of damage taken from Special attacks. However, some moves have priority changes that allow them to be performed in a specific order regardless of the Speed stat.

input: How many different natures can a Pokémon have?
output: An individual Pokémon can have one of 25 possible natures. These natures are randomly determined for each Pokémon.

input: How do natures affect a Pokémon's stat growth?
output: Twenty of the available natures influence stat growth. These specific natures increase one stat by 10% while decreasing another stat by 10%.

input: Can I change the nature of my Pokémon once it is determined?
output: No, the nature of an individual Pokémon cannot be changed. It is randomly determined and remains permanent.

input: What are Individual Values (IVs) in the game?
output: Individual Values are secret values that determine how a Pokémon's stats grow innately. Because these values differ for each individual Pokémon, two Pokémon of the same nature, level, and species may have slightly different stats.

input: What is the range of an IV for a specific stat, and which value is most beneficial?
output: Each stat has an IV that ranges from 0 to 31. A value of 31 is the most beneficial as it provides the most stat growth.

input: Can a player change the IVs of a Pokémon once they are determined?
output: No, the IVs of an individual Pokémon cannot be changed. These values are randomly determined for each Pokémon.

input: What are Effort Values and how do they affect a Pokémon?
output: Effort Values are secret values that influence how a Pokémon's stats grow based on the opponents it fights. These stats are added to the Pokémon whenever it levels up.

input: How can I increase a specific stat for my Pokémon through battling?
output: You should fight Pokémon species that have an EV yield for the stat you wish to increase. For example, fighting wild Oddish will provide +1 Sp. Atk to the Pokémon that defeats it.

input: What is the relationship between Effort Values and stat increases at level 100?
output: At level 100, roughly 4 EVs in a specific stat are equivalent to a +1 increase in that stat.

input: What are the limits on how many Effort Values a Pokémon can have?
output: A Pokémon can have a maximum of 255 EVs in a single stat. Additionally, there is an overall limit of 510 EVs across all stats.

input: How do vitamin items work for training Effort Values?
output: Items such as Protein, Carbos, and HP Up can be used to increase a stat's EVs by 10. However, these items cannot be used once the affected stat has reached 100 EVs.

input: How many moves can a Pokémon know at once?
output: A Pokémon is limited to knowing up to four moves at a time. This restriction creates a limited space that helps determine the individual Pokémon's play style.

input: Why are moves considered the most important tools for a Pokémon?
output: Moves are arguably the most important tools because they essentially determine what a Pokémon is capable of doing during a battle.

input: How is the category of an attack determined in this game?
output: The category of an attack is determined by its type. This determines whether a move utilizes the Attack or Sp. Atk stat.

input: Which move types are considered physical?
output: Physical types include Bug, Flying, Fighting, Ghost, Normal, Poison, Steel, Ground, and Rock. Moves of these types use the Attack stat.

input: Which move types are considered special?
output: Special types include Psychic, Fire, Grass, Water, Electric, Ice, Dark, and Dragon. Moves of these types use the Sp. Atk stat.

input: Why would a Fighting-type Machamp be more effective than a Water-type Kingler if both have high Attack stats?
output: Machamp is better off because Fighting is a physical type, meaning its STAB moves utilize its higher Attack stat. In contrast, Kingler is a Water-type, which is a special type, and therefore cannot utilize its high Attack stat for those moves.

input: How can a Pokémon learn a move it previously learned through leveling up?
output: You should visit the Move Reminder NPC located on Two Island. This NPC can teach a Pokémon a previously learned level-up move in exchange for either one Big Mushroom or two TinyMushrooms per move.

input: What is the difference between TMs and HMs when teaching moves?
output: TMs are single-use items that teach a specific move based on compatibility. HMs can be used repeatedly to teach moves, but unlike TMs, they cannot be replaced by another move.

input: What happens when a Pokémon evolves into a species that learns a move at that specific evolution level?
output: The Pokémon will attempt to learn that move immediately after the evolution process occurs. This is part of the standard leveling up process for learning moves.

input: How do Move Tutors function in the Kanto region and Sevii Islands?
output: Various NPCs act as Move Tutors who can teach a unique move to a Pokémon one time. Most of the moves taught by these NPCs were TMs in the original Pokémon Red and Blue games.

input: How can moves be passed from one Pokémon to another through breeding?
output: When breeding for eggs, certain compatible moves known by the father can be passed down to the child Pokémon.

input: What are the different ways a Pokémon can learn new moves?
output: Pokémon can learn moves by leveling up, using TMs or HMs, or learning from a Move Tutor. Additionally, moves can be passed down through breeding or taught by the Move Reminder.

input: What happens when a Pokémon tries to learn a new move but already knows four moves?
output: One of the existing moves must be forgotten to make room for the new one. This process is necessary because a Pokémon can only know a maximum of four moves.

input: Can HM moves be forgotten naturally when learning a new move?
output: No, HM moves cannot be forgotten naturally in this manner. You will need an alternative method to remove them from a Pokémon's move set.

input: How can I delete an HM move from my Pokémon?
output: Travel to Fuchsia City to find an NPC known as the Move Deleter. This character can delete any of your Pokémon's moves, including those learned via HMs.

input: Where is the Move Deleter located and what is their function?
output: The Move Deleter is located in Fuchsia City. This NPC provides a service that allows you to delete any move from your Pokémon at any time.

input: What is the purpose of a Pokémon's Ability?
output: A Pokémon's Ability provides a passive effect that can occur in the overworld or during battle. These effects often influence a species' defensive or offensive capabilities, which can help inform potential strategies when using them.

input: How many abilities can an individual Pokémon have?
output: An individual Pokémon can have one of up to two abilities. The specific abilities available are determined by the Pokémon's species.

input: What is the effect of certain moves and Abilities on Pokémon?
output: Some moves and Abilities have the capacity to inflict status conditions on Pokémon. These conditions typically serve to hinder the targeted Pokémon in some way.

input: What are the effects of the Burn status condition and how is it treated?
output: A Pokémon with Burn will have its Attack stat halved and lose 1/8 of its max HP every turn. You can typically cure this condition using a Burn Heal.

input: How does Poison differ from Bad poison in terms of HP loss?
output: Regular Poison causes a consistent loss of 1/8 max HP per turn. Bad poison starts by decreasing 1/16 of max HP, but this damage increases by an additional 1/16 for every turn the Pokémon remains in the condition.

input: What happens to a Pokémon with the Poison status condition when it is outside of battle?
output: Outside of battle, a poisoned Pokémon will lose 1 HP for every four steps it takes. If the condition is not healed, the Pokémon will eventually faint.

input: What occurs when a Pokémon affected by Bad poison switches out at the end of a battle?
output: When a Pokémon with Bad poison switches out at the end of a battle, the condition transforms into regular poison. It can then be cured using the same methods used for regular poison.

input: How does the Sleep status affect a Pokémon and what item can be used to cure it?
output: A sleeping Pokémon is unable to move for 1 to 4 turns before waking up. This condition is typically cured by using an Awakening.

input: How does the move Rest interact with the Sleep status?
output: Using the move Rest will cause the user to be inflicted with the Sleep status. This specific instance of sleep lasts for a set duration of 2 turns.

input: Under what conditions can a frozen Pokémon be thawed?
output: A frozen Pokémon may thaw naturally with a 20% chance during any turn, or it can be thawed by being hit by a Fire-type attack. Alternatively, you can typically use an Ice Heal to cure it.

input: Can a Pokémon be frozen if there is harsh sunlight?
output: No, Pokémon cannot be frozen while under the effects of harsh sunlight.

input: What are the penalties for a Pokémon suffering from Paralysis?
output: Paralysis reduces a Pokémon's Speed stat to 25% and creates a 25% chance that the Pokémon will fail to use its move. This status is typically cured with a Parlyz Heal.

input: Which status conditions persist after a battle has ended?
output: The passage indicates that Burn, Poison, Bad poison, Sleep, Freeze, and Paralysis are status conditions that will remain even when the battle is over.

input: What happens to a Pokémon that is afflicted with Confusion?
output: A Pokémon with Confusion has a 50% chance to hurt itself. This occurs instead of the Pokémon using its intended move.

input: How does the Flinch status condition affect a Pokémon in battle?
output: When a Pokémon is inflicted with Flinch, it will instantly fail to act. This specific effect only lasts for the current turn.

input: What are the effects of the Bound status condition?
output: A Bound Pokémon cannot be switched out or flee and loses 1/16 of its max HP every turn. This condition lasts for a random duration of 2 to 5 turns.

input: What occurs when a Pokémon is Seeded?
output: A Seeded Pokémon loses 1/8 of its max HP each turn. The amount of damage the Pokémon takes is then used to heal the opponent.

input: How does the Trapped status condition work?
output: A Pokémon that is Trapped is unable to flee or be switched out. This effect persists until the opponent is switched out or faints.

input: What is the effect of Infatuation on a Pokémon?
output: Infatuation causes the afflicted Pokémon to have a 50% chance to fail when attempting to use its move.

input: Which moves can be used to reduce a Pokémon's stats, and what do they do?
output: You can use Growl to reduce a Pokémon's attack stat or Leer to reduce its defense stat. Additionally, Smoke Screen can be used to reduce the accuracy of moves.

input: Which moves can be used to increase a Pokémon's stats?
output: You can use Swords Dance to increase a Pokémon's attack stat. Alternatively, Minimize can be used to increase the chance to evade an attack.

input: When are status conditions such as stat reductions or confusion cured?
output: These status conditions are cured once the battle ends. They will also be cured if the affected Pokémon is switched out.

input: What happens when a Pokémon meets certain conditions?
output: When specific conditions are met, a Pokémon will evolve. This process transforms the Pokémon into a new species, which is typically stronger than the previous one.

input: How many times do most Pokémon evolve?
output: Most Pokémon evolve either once or twice. Additionally, some Pokémon have the ability to evolve into one of multiple different species.

input: How do most Pokémon evolve?
output: Most Pokémon evolve by reaching a preset level. Evolution occurs once they hit that specific level or any level above it.

input: What is required for Pokémon that evolve via evolution stones?
output: These specific Pokémon require the use of a certain stone item. Once the correct stone is used on the Pokémon, it will evolve.

input: Under what conditions do some Pokémon evolve through trading?
output: Certain Pokémon will only evolve after they have been traded to another player. This is the primary requirement for their evolution.

input: What are the requirements for Pokémon that evolve through high friendship?
output: These Pokémon must reach a friendship value of 220 or higher and then level up to any level. Additionally, this method of evolution is unavailable until the National Pokédex is obtained.

input: How does trading with a held item work for evolution?
output: Certain species evolve when they are traded to another player while holding a specific item. This process cannot occur until the player has obtained the National Pokédex.

input: Which evolution methods are locked until the National Pokédex is obtained?
output: Evolution via high friendship and evolution via trading while holding a specific item are both locked. You must obtain the National Pokédex before these two methods can occur.

input: How can I stop a Pokémon from evolving during the evolution process?
output: You can cancel the evolution process by pressing the B button. This action allows the Pokémon to retain its current form.

input: What item can be used to permanently prevent a Pokémon from evolving?
output: A Pokémon can hold an Everstone to stop it from evolving. This prevents evolution at all times, even if all necessary conditions for evolving have been met.

input: What are the potential downsides of evolving your Pokémon?
output: Evolving can lead to your Pokémon learning moves at later levels compared to their unevolved forms. Additionally, those that evolve using an evolution stone often learn very few or no moves through leveling up once they have evolved.

input: How does evolution via an evolution stone affect a Pokémon's move set?
output: Pokémon that evolve using an evolution stone typically learn little to no level-up moves in their evolved forms. This makes the timing of evolution important for your team's strength.

input: What should I consider before deciding to evolve my Pokémon?
output: You should determine which moves you want your Pokémon to learn before they evolve. Because you have the ability to cancel evolution, you can strategically time the process to ensure your Pokémon learns necessary moves first.

input: What are some general tips for building a successful team of six Pokémon?
output: You should focus on maintaining type variety to avoid poor matchups against certain types. Additionally, you should consider non-STAB coverage and avoid redundant coverage overlap among your team members.

input: Why is it important to have type variety on your team?
output: Having too many Pokémon of a single type can be detrimental. This can lead to your team having a very poor matchup when facing certain types.

input: What is the purpose of using non-STAB moves?
output: While STAB maximizes damage, moves that do not share a type with the user still serve a strong purpose. For instance, Normal-type Pokémon can use Bite to damage Psychic- and Ghost-types, since Normal-type STAB usually cannot damage Ghost-types.

input: How should I handle coverage overlap when choosing my team?
output: You should try to avoid having too much coverage against the same specific types to prevent redundancy. For example, if you have Electric, Water, and Grass types, you may want to replace one because Grass and Electric both cover Water, while Water and Grass both cover Rock and Ground.

input: How can I use Ground-type immunities to my advantage in battle?
output: You can use a Pokémon weak to Ground-type attacks, such as a Fire- or Electric-type, to bait the opponent into using those moves. Once the attack is baited, you can safely switch in a Pokémon that is immune to Ground-type attacks.

input: Which Pokémon are recommended for safely switching into Ground-type attacks?
output: Good choices for this role include the Flying-type Pokémon Fearow or Dodrio. Additionally, the Gengar family is a strong option because they possess the Levitate Ability.

input: How can I obtain Poké Balls in the game?
output: You can acquire Poké Balls by purchasing them at the Poké Mart. Additionally, you may find Poké Balls as you travel on your way.

input: What are the differences between the three basic types of Poké Balls?
output: The standard Poké Ball is the cheapest option and provides no extra capture chance. The Great Ball, available mid-game, offers a 50% higher capture chance, while the Ultra Ball, available later in the game, offers a 100% higher capture chance.

input: When can I get access to the new kinds of Poké Balls that offer a greater capture chance?
output: These specialized Poké Balls are only available after you gain access to the Sevii Islands. They provide a greater chance of capture provided that the conditions are appropriate.

input: Which basic Poké Ball should I use if I want the highest capture chance among the standard options?
output: You should use the Ultra Ball, as it offers a 100% higher chance to capture than the basic Poké Ball. This item becomes available during the latter part of the game.

input: How does the Great Ball compare to the standard Poké Ball in terms of effectiveness?
output: The Great Ball is available during the middle of the game. It provides a 50% higher chance to capture a Pokémon compared to the standard Poké Ball.

input: How do I initiate a battle with a wild Pokémon?
output: You can find wild Pokémon by entering the tall grass. Alternatively, you can use a "Pole" to fish or surf the seas to start a battle.

input: What are the steps to attempt to catch a wild Pokémon during a battle?
output: First, weaken the wild Pokémon. When it is your turn again, select Bag, choose a Poké Ball, and then select Use to throw the ball.

input: What does it mean if a Poké Ball does not shake after being thrown?
output: If the ball does not shake, the Pokémon may require a significant amount of weakening before it can be captured.

input: What should I do if the Poké Ball shakes twice?
output: A ball that shakes twice indicates you are making progress. You may be able to capture the Pokémon by using a better ball.

input: What is the significance of a Poké Ball shaking three times?
output: This means you are almost successful. The Pokémon might need Attracting so that it hardly attacks you.

input: How do I know if I have successfully captured a Pokémon?
output: A successful capture occurs when the ball shakes three times, does not shake again, and is followed by a clicking lock.

input: What happens immediately after a Pokémon is captured?
output: The game will ask, "Will you give a nickname." You can select YES to provide a name or select NO to decline.

input: How can I change a Pokémon's nickname after it has been caught?
output: You must visit the name rater's house located in Lavender Town. He will enable you to give your Pokémon a new nickname.

input: What are Abilities in the game and how do they function?
output: Abilities are passive effects that vary depending on the Pokémon. These effects can be active during battle or while in the overworld.

input: Can a Pokémon's Ability be changed once it has been determined?
output: No, an individual Pokémon can only have one Ability at a time. This Ability cannot be changed.

input: How many different Abilities can a single Pokémon species potentially have?
output: A species may be capable of having one of two possible Abilities. For instance, a Diglett could have either Arena Trap or Sand Veil.

input: Under what circumstances can a Pokémon acquire a new Ability?
output: A Pokémon may gain a new Ability through evolution. This occurs if the ability in its slot differs in the evolved form of the species.

input: Where does the adventure begin and who will I meet there?
output: Your journey starts in Pallet Town. In this location, you will be welcomed by the famous Professor Oak.

input: What happens after the introduction in Pallet Town?
output: After the introduction, you will meet your very first Pokémon. From there, you will head off into your journey throughout the Kanto region.

input: What is the ultimate goal of the journey through Kanto?
output: The goal of traveling throughout the Kanto region is to become the best Pokémon Trainer ever.

input: What should I do before leaving my bedroom?
output: You should withdraw the Potion from your computer. This is a precaution in case your rival puts up a good fight.

input: Where can I go to heal my Pokémon for free?
output: You can go downstairs to see your Mom. She will heal your Pokémon if they get tired.

input: Who lives in Pallet Town?
output: Pallet Town is home to you, your mom, your rival, and his sister Daisy. The town also houses the Pokémon Research Laboratory.

input: Who is Professor Oak?
output: Professor Oak is the head of the Pokémon Research Laboratory and is world renowned for his Pokémon studies. He is also the grandfather of your rival.

input: What happens when I first try to look inside Professor Oak's Laboratory?
output: You may look inside the Laboratory, but you will find that Professor Oak is away. He appears to have left town.

input: How do I obtain my first Pokémon?
output: First, step outside of town to search for Professor Oak, who will call out to warn you. Once you assemble with him and your rival, he will offer you a choice of three Pokémon.

input: How does my choice of starter Pokémon affect my rival?
output: Your choice of starter determines which Pokémon your rival will select. The rival will always choose a Pokémon that contrasts with the one you picked.

input: Does choosing a specific starter Pokémon impact the end of the game?
output: Yes, your initial choice determines which Legendary Beast Pokémon is released at the end of the game.

input: Which starter Pokémon is recommended for advanced players and why?
output: Charmander may be more appropriate for advanced players. This is because it will struggle when facing the first two Gym leaders.

input: Is one starter Pokémon objectively better than the others?
output: No, none of the options are bad or worse than the others. All three Pokémon are perfectly viable for the entire game, and players should choose based on their own taste.

input: What happens when you try to exit town with your first Pokémon?
output: Your rival will challenge you to a duel to test his mettle. You cannot refuse this battle before you are allowed to leave town.

input: Why might the first battle with your rival be difficult?
output: The match can be tricky because your rival chooses the Pokémon that has an advantage over yours. However, he does not always make the best choices, which can give you the upper hand.

input: What can you do if your Pokémon runs low on hit points during the rival battle?
output: You may use the Potion that was withdrawn from the computer to heal your Pokémon. Some players choose not to use healing items for a more wholesome challenge, as the game is not too difficult.

input: What are the consequences of losing the match against your rival?
output: Losing the match is not too severe. You simply miss out on a free level up and your rival's 80.

input: Where do you go once the battle with your rival is finished?
output: After the battle is over, you are ready to leave town. You should then travel along Route 1.

input: Who is Daisy and how does she feel about the player?
output: Daisy is the sister of your lifelong rival. Unlike your rival, who carries a grudge and downplays you, Daisy is nice and thinks you are OK.

input: How can you obtain a Town Map?
output: After you return from Viridian City, visit the home located just above the Laboratory. Daisy will be there to give you a Town Map.

input: What should I do if my Pokémon faints during my journey to Viridian City?
output: You have two options if your Pokémon faints. You can head back home to receive care from Mom, or you can continue traveling to Viridian City and visit its Pokémon Center.

input: Where should I go to continue my journey?
output: You should resume your journey by traveling north. Your destination is Viridian City.

input: Can I capture new Pokémon while traveling to Viridian City?
output: No, you cannot capture new Pokémon at this time. Instead, you should use this opportunity to increase your Pokémon's experience levels.

input: What should I do if I encounter a battle that is too difficult for my Pokémon?
output: If you find yourself in a battle that is too challenging, you should use the Run command. This will allow you to escape the fight.

input: Where do I start my journey and which direction should I travel?
output: You begin your journey at the bottom of route #1. From there, you must travel north to reach Viridian City.

input: What should I do when I encounter the man on Route 1?
output: You should speak with the man you encounter on the route. He will offer you a free Potion, which you should make sure to collect.

input: How can I avoid fighting wild Pokémon on Route 1?
output: To avoid battles, spend as little time as possible walking through the grassy areas. These are the only locations where wild Pokémon lurk and where you are at risk of being attacked.

input: What is the best strategy for battling wild Pidgeys and Rattatas if I don't have Poké Balls?
output: Since you cannot catch them, fighting these Pokémon is only useful for gaining EXP. Stick to using your regular damage-dealing attacks and be careful that the wild Pokémon do not wear you down.

input: What can I do at the Pokémon Center in Viridian City?
output: You can visit the Pokémon Center to restore your Pokémon to full health. This is the first Pokémon Center you will encounter in the game.

input: What is available at the Viridian City Poké Mart?
output: The Poké Mart stocks various items that are useful for Pokémon trainers. Additionally, this specific Mart offers a delivery service.

input: How can I help the Poké Mart in Viridian City?
output: The Poké Mart has a delivery service that requires your assistance. You will need to help them by making a special delivery.

input: What services are available at the Pokémon Center in Viridian City?
output: You can visit Nurse Joy to have all of your Pokémon healed for free. Additionally, the center provides computers that allow you to change your Pokémon roster and access your item storage.
